title: Stopped by traffic police and asked for documents
triggers: traffic police stopped me and asked for licence
cop asking for RC and insurance
I don't have my licence with me
police ne gaadi roki documents maang rahe hain

rights.plain_explanation: You must show your driving licence when a police officer in uniform asks for it in a public place.
If a document isn't with you, the law lets you produce copies within fifteen days of the demand.
Your licence and RC in DigiLocker or mParivahan count as valid, the same as the paper originals. Officers can verify them on the app.

do_now: Pull over safely and stay polite.
Show your licence and RC in DigiLocker or mParivahan if you don't have paper copies.
If there's a fine, ask for an official e-challan or a printed receipt. Don't hand over cash without one.
Note the officer's name and the time and place.
user_at_fault_cases: Driving with no licence at all (not even digitally): a challan is lawful. Pay it through the official challan and keep the receipt.
An expired document can also be challaned. Renew it and pay the fine officially.

escalation.label: Check or contest the challan
escalation.detail: Every e-challan appears on the Virtual Courts portal. You can pay it there or choose to contest it.

escalation.label: Free legal aid
escalation.detail: Call NALSA on 15100 or visit your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the district court. Women, children, people in custody and people below the income limit get a free lawyer.
